scripts.lint: node apps/api/scripts/check-harnesses.mjs && node tools/check-decisions-index.mjs && node tools/build-decisions-triggers.mjs --check && node tools/check-smoke-folds.mjs && turbo run lint --filter=!web
scripts._lint:decisions_index_why: DECISIONS-INDEX.md points at DECISIONS.md BY LINE NUMBER, and a line number moves when anything is inserted above it — the index's own header says so and tells the reader to re-derive numbers by hand, i.e. it documents a hazard nothing could detect. :10726 Low-1 recorded the consequence: a citation went stale inside the commit that moved it and FAILED SILENTLY BY LANDING ON A REAL HEADING. Measured 2026-08-27 before anything was changed: 212 pointers, 193 correct, 19 wrong — 13 of them landing inside the decision BEFORE the one they named, one 158 lines in. Runs at the ROOT before turbo for the same reason as the harness check above: a guard a warm cache can skip is not a guard. Neither this nor any lint task reads the two files, so nothing else in the repo could ever have caught this.
scripts._lint:decisions_triggers_why: DECISIONS-TRIGGERS.md is GENERATED from the `Read before ...` sentences the rulings write about themselves, and it is one of the three files the grounding rule says a chat reads EVERY session. A stale one is worse than none: it would quietly answer `nothing binds your task` for a ruling added since it was last built, which is :19256's recorded failure (a chat grepped the wrong vocabulary and re-opened a settled question with Kd). --check regenerates in memory and fails if the committed file differs, so adding a ruling without rebuilding cannot merge. Runs at the ROOT before turbo for the same reason as the two checks above: a guard a warm cache can skip is not a guard.
scripts._lint:smoke_folds_why: A fold changes what a TESTER sees without changing what any test asserts, and jsdom has no layout, so the suite is structurally blind to it — the only readers who can be wrong about a folded surface are the smoke sheets, and they are prose. Measured 2026-09-04 before this guard existed: smoke-attendance.md carried FOUR wrong steps naming content behind an unopened fold, while smoke-gym-hours-fold.md told the same tester that seeing that content without tapping was the failure it was built to catch — two live sheets, one screen, opposite expectations. Fourth recurrence of the class (:32498, :33265 §1, :33334 C/H-1, this), and the first mechanical check on it: :33334's standing rule greps RUNBOOK/ when a commit REMOVES a surface, and :32929 removed nothing, it HID something. Runs at the ROOT before turbo for the same reason as the three checks above: a guard a warm cache can skip is not a guard.
scripts._lint:harness_why: T3 round 5, Low-6. The harness parse check used to be a step inside api's own lint script, where it inherited that task's turbo cache — 172 inputs, NONE outside apps/api (measured with `turbo run lint --dry=json`). So breaking any of the 16 harnesses that live in apps/web, packages/ or root tools/ left the cache valid and a warm `turbo run lint` replayed a pass without ever running the check. Rounds 2 and 3 were harness-only fix rounds, i.e. exactly the case it misses. It runs HERE, before turbo, so no cache can decide whether it happened. The check itself explains what it guards (apps/api/scripts/check-harnesses.mjs).
